Introduction to Macon County, Missouri and This Tax Sale Guide

Macon County sits in north central Missouri. It is known for farmland, lakes, and a strong rural community. The county seat is the city of Macon. Local government services are managed from the Macon County Courthouse.

This guide explains how the Macon County tax sale works. It covers the auction date, location, bidding rules, and redemption period. You will also learn how investors participate and what returns may occur.

The goal is simple. Help investors understand Macon County tax lien certificates and how the sale works. All details come from official county or state sources whenever possible.

What Is Macon County’s Tax Lien Investing System?

Macon County uses a tax lien certificate sale system. When property taxes stay unpaid, the county sells a lien certificate at a public auction. The winning bidder pays the delinquent taxes and receives a certificate of purchase.

The property owner then has time to repay the taxes and interest. This is called the redemption period. If the owner redeems the property, the investor receives the investment plus interest. If the owner does not redeem, the investor may apply for a tax deed after the required process.

Important Details About Macon County Tax Sales

Key Takeaways
  • Macon County, Missouri hosts an annual tax lien certificate sale, typically on the fourth Monday in August.
  • Investors purchase tax lien certificates by paying delinquent taxes, and property owners have a redemption period to reclaim their property.
  • The tax lien investing system offers potential returns of about 10 percent annually if property owners redeem their taxes.
  • Due diligence is essential, involving research on property conditions, titles, and values before participating in the auction.
  • Macon County provides a stable investment environment due to its affordable real estate market and regular auction opportunities.

Recent example: A recent sale took place in late August at 10 AM according to county postings.

Missouri law sets the typical schedule for county tax sales on the fourth Monday in August.

Fun Facts About Macon County

  • Macon County has a population of about 15,000 residents.
  • The county was formed in the early nineteenth century and named after Nathaniel Macon.
  • Farming is the main industry. Corn and soybeans are common crops.
  • Long Branch Lake State Park sits inside the county and attracts many visitors each year.

Real estate values in the county remain affordable. Rural land and small town housing dominate the market. This often creates entry points for investors at tax sales.

Why Macon County Is Ideal for Tax Lien Investors

  • Affordable property market makes entry costs lower than large cities.
  • State tax lien opportunities exist every year through the annual auction.
  • High returns may reach the statutory redemption interest rate.
  • Low risk investment structure since the lien is secured by real estate.
  • Rural counties often have fewer bidders which may reduce competition.

Auction Process for Tax Lien Sales in Macon County

Missouri counties conduct tax lien auctions under state statute Chapter 140. The county collector manages the sale and publishes the list of delinquent properties before the auction.

In Macon County, the sale is usually held at the courthouse and conducted in person.

When Are Macon County Tax Sales Held?

The Macon County tax sale normally occurs on the fourth Monday in August each year. The auction begins at about 10:00 AM Central Time.

Where Is the Auction Held?

The auction takes place at the Macon County Courthouse.

Address
101 East Washington Street
Macon, Missouri

The county collector oversees the event and handles payments.

Is Registration Required?

Most Missouri counties require bidders to register and sign affidavits before bidding. Investors usually confirm they do not owe delinquent taxes in the county.

Registration details and paperwork are provided through the county collector’s office.

How the Auction Works

Typical tax lien auction process

  • The collector announces the parcel number and legal description.
  • The opening bid equals delinquent taxes, interest, and costs.
  • Bidders compete by offering a higher premium above the opening amount.
  • The highest bidder wins the lien certificate.
  • Payment is due immediately after the auction closes.
  • The county issues a certificate of purchase to the winning bidder.
  • The property owner may redeem the property by repaying taxes plus interest.

If the property remains unredeemed after the required process, the certificate holder may apply for a collector’s deed.

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns

Missouri tax lien certificates can produce solid returns. Interest rates may reach about 10 percent annually during the redemption period.

The final return depends on several factors.

  • Whether the property owner redeems the property
  • How long the redemption takes
  • Additional taxes paid by the investor during the holding period

Investors may also collect interest on subsequent tax payments. Missouri law allows around 8 percent interest on later taxes paid by the certificate holder.

If redemption does not occur, the investor may obtain a tax deed after completing required notices and a title search.

Open to All Investors Including Foreign Buyers

Missouri tax sales are open to most investors. Both local and out of state buyers can participate in the auction.

Some rules apply.

  • Investors must register before bidding.
  • Buyers confirm they have no delinquent taxes in the county.
  • Out of state buyers may need to appoint a local agent for legal service.

This structure allows global investment opportunities in Missouri tax lien certificates. Many investors travel across states to attend auctions.

Foreign investors also participate by working with local partners or representatives.

Importance of Due Diligence in Macon County Tax Lien Investing

Tax lien investing is secure compared with many investments. Still, research is important before bidding.

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Review the delinquent property list before the sale.
  • Check the county GIS map for location details.
  • Inspect the property if possible.
  • Review title records and existing liens.
  • Estimate property value and market demand.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • Property may have environmental problems.
  • Land may be landlocked or unusable.
  • Structures may be damaged or unsafe.
  • Other liens may exist that survive the tax sale.

Careful research helps avoid these problems.

Why Macon County Is a Strong Choice for Tax Lien Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • Stable agriculture economy in north Missouri
  • Low property values create lower entry bids
  • Regular annual tax sale provides predictable investment opportunities
  • Real estate backed liens reduce investment risk

Real Estate Market Overview

  • Housing prices remain affordable compared with national averages.
  • Many parcels sold at tax sales are vacant lots or rural land.
  • Investors often find long term land investments through tax sales.
  • Some buyers hold property for hunting land or farmland.

Conclusion

Macon County, Missouri holds a yearly tax lien certificate sale to recover unpaid property taxes. The auction usually occurs on the fourth Monday in August at the county courthouse.

Investors bid on tax lien certificates. The winning bidder pays the delinquent taxes and receives a certificate of purchase. Property owners then have time to redeem the property by repaying taxes and interest.

Interest rates can reach about ten percent annually. This makes tax lien investing attractive for many buyers.

Still, research matters. Property condition, location, and title issues must be reviewed before bidding.

With careful planning, Macon County tax lien certificates can offer stable returns backed by real estate.

Pro Tips for Macon County Tax Lien Investors

  • Visit the courthouse before the auction to review posted property lists.
  • Drive by rural parcels when possible. Some may lack road access.
  • Bring certified funds. Payment is usually due right after the auction.
  • Study farmland values since many parcels are agricultural land.
  • Watch parcels that appear multiple years in a row. These sometimes offer lower competition.

FAQs About Macon County Tax Lien Certificates

Do investors receive the property immediately after the auction?

No. The owner still has a redemption period before a deed can be issued.

Who pays property taxes during the redemption period?

The certificate holder often pays future taxes to protect the investment.

Can a property have other liens?

Yes. Some liens may survive the tax sale depending on the type.

Is quiet title required after receiving a deed?

Many investors complete a quiet title action before selling the property.

Can investors sell the certificate to another buyer?

In some cases the certificate may be assigned to another investor.
